subject: Error when fitting fully constrained model of covariance; No Chi Square, Model not fit

messages.author: 6ae7bf04b963222b
messages.subject: Error when fitting fully constrained model of covariance; No Chi Square, Model not fit
parts:
Hello,

I have a question. I'm trying to fit a fully constrained covariance model with varying degrees of misspecification to obtain chi square fit values.
However, when I try to fit the model I encounter the following problem (please see example syntax below). I don't have this problem when using Mplus, so I suspect this is a problem with my specification or a model argument that I am missing. 


#Demonstration of problem

library(lavaan)

m1 <- rnorm(100,0,1)
m2 <- rnorm(100,0,1)
m3 <- rnorm(100,0,1)
d <- data.frame(m1,m2,m3)

m1 <- '
m1 ~~ .2*m2 + .2*m3;
m2 ~~ .2*m3;
m1 ~~ 1.2*m1;
m2 ~~ 1.2*m2;
m3 ~~ 1.2*m3;
'
#A fully constrained covariance matrix essentially
#with misspecification

fit1 <- sem(m1, data = d, meanstructure = FALSE)
summary(fit1, fit.measures=TRUE)
#Warning, model not fit, Estimates below are simply starting values
#I did not enter starting values, I entered constraints
#Advised to refit model with test="standard"

fit2 <- sem(m1, data = d, meanstructure = FALSE, test="standard")
summary(fit2, fit.measures=TRUE)
#Identical warning and advice, no difference

#Note that if I use Mplus, I can fit this fully constrained model
#without any difficulty. The challenge is that this is part of a larger
#simulation study and I'm using a server computer which does not have
#Mplus.

#ANY SUGGESTIONS, COMMENTS, ETC. ARE GREATLY APPRECIATED!!!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Error when fitting fully constrained model of covariance; No Chi Square, Model not fit
parts:
I'm guessing this is an artifact of not giving the optimizer anything to do.  That is, you aren't actually estimating anything if all the parameters are fixed.  I suppose Mplus might  have programmed a check for such a case, where they skip the optimizer and just use the fixed parameters as the final solution, and perhaps Yves hasn't included such a check.  He's on sabbatical, so it might be a while until you hear a response, but for your simulation, you could just calculate the chi-squared yourself manually:

Sigma <- fitted(fit1)$cov
S <- cov(d)
ChiSq <- log(det(Sigma)) - log(det(S)) + sum(diag(S %*% solve(Sigma))) - nrow(S)

Then you can look up formulas to calculate any other ChiSq-based indices you want.  For CFI/TLI, you can grab the ChiSq of the baseline model from another lavaan object where you actually have estimates (or just fit your own baseline model).  Bollen's SRMR is pretty easy to calculate:

corResiduals <- diag(diag(solve(S))) %*% resid(fit1)$cov %*% diag(diag(solve(S)))
mean(lav_matrix_vech(corResiduals))

You can look up the source code if you want to see how he calculates anything.

Terry

Terry's suggestion is a better way to proceed.  However, if you want something from lavaan to check it against, I was able to get a chi-square for your model from lavaan by running a two group analysis with one parameter free in the second group.  The summary provides separate chi-square values for each group.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Error when fitting fully constrained model of covariance; No Chi Square, Model not fit
parts:
On 03/24/2016 11:00 PM, Joseph Gonzales wrote:
> Hello,
>
> I have a question. I'm trying to fit a fully constrained covariance
> model with varying degrees of misspecification to obtain chi square fit
> values.

The logic used by lavaan is the following: first check if the optimizer
has converged; if yes, show test statistic; if not, do not show a test
statstic. If there are no free parameters, the optimizer is not needed,
so no convergence can occur...

There is a workaround (not documented, and it may change in the future):

fit <- sem(m1, data = d, meanstructure = FALSE,
control=list(optim.force.converged = TRUE))

to 'fake' convergence, and get a chi-square test.

Yves.

messages.author: 6ae7bf04b963222b
messages.subject: Re: Error when fitting fully constrained model of covariance; No Chi Square, Model not fit
parts:
Thank you Terrence, Markus, and Yves for your prompt replies! This is extremely helpful. I did have a follow-up question, however, based on responses from Terrence and Yves.

Returning to my previous example with a seed added for consistency in the discussion and some additional syntax given input from Terrence and Yves.

If I estimate the fit function (Terrence's suggestion) and multiply by my sample size minus one (N-1), then I get a chi square value very close to that produced by lavaan, but there is a slight discrepancy. Yves, I was wondering if you could comment on what the difference is; how is lavaan's chi square scaled?

Again, much thanks to everyone for helping me on this problem.

Joe

#Syntax

set.seed(32516)

fit1 <- sem(m1, data = d, meanstructure = FALSE,
control=list(optim.force.converged = TRUE))
summary(fit1, fit.measures=TRUE)

lavChiSq <- fitMeasures(fit1)[c("chisq")]; lavChiSq
#This is the lavaan ChiSq when using argument
#That model converged

#If I were to estimate ChiSq using the model and observed cov matrices
C <- fitted(fit1)$cov; C
S <- cov(d); S

n <- dim(S)[1]; n
N <- dim(d)[1]; N

#Without scaling of number of observation, Fit function
fitf <- log(det(C)) - log(det(S)) + sum(diag(S %*% solve(C))) - n
fitf

#W/ sample df times fit function
ChiSq <- (N-1)*(log(det(C)) - log(det(S)) + sum(diag(S %*% solve(C))) - n)
ChiSq

fitf; ChiSq; lavChiSq

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Error when fitting fully constrained model of covariance; No Chi Square, Model not fit
parts:
On 03/25/2016 06:22 PM, Joseph Gonzales wrote:
> #W/ sample df times fit function
> ChiSq <- (N-1)*(log(det(C)) - log(det(S)) + sum(diag(S %*% solve(C))) - n)

Simply use N (instead of N-1) as the multiplier. This is the 'normal
likelihood' way which is the default in lavaan. There is also the
'wishart' way, which would imply N-1.

Yves.
